title: AI Medical Interpreter Bias Audit: Clinical Guide
summary: Audit AI medical interpretation by language, dialect, accent, clinical error severity, workflow conditions, security, and escalation paths.
body_markdown:
###


A clinical AI interpreter bias audit should measure clinically meaningful errors by language, dialect, accent, audio condition, encounter type, and error severity. For a U.S. healthcare deployment, report omissions, additions, number and medication errors, subgroup sample sizes, uncertainty, and the workflow conditions used for testing.


###


A healthcare organization should test every language and dialect it plans to use within the pilot scope, prioritizing high-volume and clinically consequential workflows. U.S. healthcare leaders should not treat strong results in one language as evidence for another language, dialect, patient population, audio environment, or encounter type.


###


The audit should compare the same clinical scenarios, scoring rubric, audio conditions, and error-severity rules across groups. Report subgroup sample sizes and confidence limits, and investigate large gaps rather than averaging them into one overall score that can hide uneven performance.


###


No. Opalite Health’s blinded validation is limited to Spanish, Mandarin, and Cantonese under the tested study conditions. A healthcare organization should run deployment-specific testing for other languages, dialects, populations, devices, and clinical workflows before using those settings in patient care.


###


A healthcare organization should repeat targeted testing after material model, language, device, integration, or workflow changes and on a documented monitoring schedule. In U.S. clinical use, complaints, safety events, new language expansion, or a meaningful performance shift should also trigger reassessment of the affected scope.
